title: Not to Condemn the Sons of Men
description: Not to Condemn the Sons of Men in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER NEW, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book I, collected from the Scriptures, hymn 100, headed “Believe and be saved, John 3. 16 17 18”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Long Metre (8.8.8.8). This page sets the words to WINCHESTER NEW; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Not to con-demn the sons of men Did Christ, the Son of God, ap-pear; No wea-pons in his hands are seen, No fla-ming sword, nor thun-der there.

lines: Not to condemn the sons of men
Did Christ, the Son of God, appear;
No weapons in his hands are seen,
No flaming sword, nor thunder there.
Such was the pity of our God,
He lov'd the race of man so well,
He sent his Son to bear our load
Of sins, and save our souls from hell.
Trust in his mighty name and live;
A thousand joys his lips afford,
His hands a thousand blessings give.
On rebels who refuse the grace;
The hottest hell shall be their place.

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to WINCHESTER NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
